title: When life changes
hookLine: marriage, loss, moving, retiring: revise the rule, the way the rabbis revised Jewish practice after the Temple fell
tomorrow: a monk practiced until his feet bled. what did the Buddha ask him?

cards: A job offer in another city. A wedding. A retirement party.

Some changes rearrange every day of the week, and the old routine no longer fits the new life. Jewish history holds a change like that. The Temple in Jerusalem, the center of worship, was destroyed by Rome.
Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai was walking with his student, Rabbi Joshua, past the ruins. Joshua looked and cried out: woe to us, the place where Israel's wrongs were atoned for is destroyed.

teach.b: Yohanan answered: my son, don't grieve. We have another atonement just as good: acts of loving-kindness.

teach.h: I DESIRED MERCY, AND NOT SACRIFICE.
teach.b: As the prophet Hosea says, "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice." The Hebrew word there is chesed, steady loving-kindness.

The story comes from a rabbinic collection called Avot de-Rabbi Natan, and it marks a real turn in Judaism. With the Temple gone, the rabbis didn't throw out the covenant, and they didn't pretend nothing had changed.
The Talmud ties the daily prayers to the times of the old offerings. Study of Torah, and kindness, carried what the altar had carried.
And one saying goes further: while the Temple stood, the altar atoned for Israel; now a person's table does. The family meal, with a guest at it, became a small altar.
That's the teaching: Judaism kept its purpose and rebuilt its practice to fit a life without the Temple. For a rule of your own, the same move is open. When life changes, the rule changes with it.
Keep what the old practice was for.

how: Jewish practice after the Temple's destruction centers on prayer at set times, Torah study, and acts of loving-kindness, and the family table is honored as a place of blessing and welcome. On a personal rule, a life change is a moment to rewrite the rule's form around the same purposes.

practice: Name one change in your life, coming or already here. Then name one part of your rule it breaks, and one way to revise that part so its purpose stays. Hold that small plan in mind until the bell.
